title.narrative: UNHCR Enhanced sustainability& conds for return to Syria for refugees in Lebanon
UNHCRStärkt hållbarhet&förutsättningar för återvändande för flyktingar i Libanon

description.narrative:
The intervention aims to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the situation for Syrian refugees in Lebanon by promoting and enabling their formal inclusion, strengthening the protection environment, and supporting peaceful coexistence between refugees and host communities. Through a focus on registration and civil documentation, capacity building of case management infrastructure, and long-term development of social services and local institutions the programme aims to address the legal, bureaucratic, social and financial barriers forcing Syrian refugees to live in informality and marginalisation.
Whilst rooted in the humanitarian response, the contribution in question endeavours to take a resilience approach and acknowledging the protracted nature of the crisis.
The programme is divided into two outcome areas each with an overarching objective. These are as follows:
1. Access to registration and documentation: Accurate refugee data collected through registration centres is actively used to ensure equal and transparent access to protection and service provision and registration for Syrians is allowed to resume, allowing for individual documentation and enhanced protection.
2. Safety, Protection and Access to Justice: Barrier to accessing legal remedies and documentation are reduced. Persons with special needs (PwSN) exposure to protection risks is mitigated and their needs addressed. The risk of GBV are reduced and GBV survivors have access to timely, safe and quality services and prevention and risk mitigation interventions continue. Children are protected from abuse, neglect, violence and exploitation.

För att ’stärka kapacitet i Libanon för en hållbar situation för flyktingar och värdsamhällen’ (strategimål 3.3 i den regionala Syrienkrisstrategin 2024 – 2026) har Sida i samarbete med UNHCR utvecklat en flerårig insats som ämnar långsiktigt stärka syriska flyktingars inkludering och skydd, samt motverka spänningar mellan flyktingar och lokalsamhällen. Insatsen har ett starkt fokus på GBV och skydd av barn. Insatsen ska främja inkludering av syriska flyktingar i Libanon genom ett fokus på registrering, dokumentation, och juridiskt stöd; stärka skyddsmiljön genom investeringar i s.k. 'case management'; och motverka lokala spänningar genom småskaliga infrastrukturprojekt i lokalsamhällen som tagit emot stort antal flyktingar.

The project responds to the increasing need for targeted protection and assistance of Syrian refugees in Lebanon while promoting an enabling legal and protection environment, supporting a peaceful coexistence of refugees and host communities. The contribution includes a specific focus on GBV and child protection.. Registration and civil documentation are crucial for enabling refugees to realize their rights, as it ensures access to legal residency and reduces the risk of arrest and deportation. The absence of legal status limits access to employment, education, and healthcare. Moreover, bureaucratic obstacles in obtaining or renewing residency further impede their access to essential services, leaving them in a precarious position. With the increasingly challenging environment, refugees with specific needs, children and GBV survivors will benefit from individual case management, to help them avoid having to resort to harmful coping strategies. These individual approaches are completed by the longer-term community support projects designed to transition from emergency aid to sustainable development by strengthening local infrastructure and services in areas heavily impacted by the refugee crisis.

description.narrative:
Noteworthy results achieved during 2025:
- Through the implementation of agile verification and population tracking modalities, UNHCR reached 94% of the registered population to confirm presence in Lebanon or departure. This exceeded the output target of 80% and significantly strengthened confidence in population figures, enabling more accurate targeting and planning. Given the fluid nature of population movements and the necessity to maintain confidence and integrity of refugee data as a common tool for partner response, the presence confirmation was timely and comprehensive.
- By the end of 2025, 21,692 refugees had been assisted (6,591 under SIDA) in obtaining key civil documents, including birth, marriage, and death certificates. This contributed to mitigating protection risks associated with the absence of legal documentation and supported access to essential services. According to the 2025 VASyR, birth registration rates continued to improve, with 53% of Syrian refugee children born in Lebanon reported as registered with the Foreigners Registry, compared to 50% in 2024. Marriage registration also showed progress, with 47% of marriages reported as registered with civil registry, up from 41% in 2024. Despite these gains, significant barriers remain, particularly related to the cost of procedures and limited awareness of registration requirements.
- UNHCR continued in 2025 to provide targeted assistance to 22,855 PWSN through established protection case management systems, including individual counselling, non-cash assistance, and structured referrals to specialized services. In line with findings from the 2025 VASyR and UNHCR protection monitoring (PM), these interventions remained a key entry point for identifying vulnerable individuals, assessing protection risks, and linking cases to available services, including legal assistance, psychosocial support, child protection services, and services for survivors of gender-based violence.
- In 2025, UNHCR and partners continued to prioritize the provision of quality GBV case management services for survivors and individuals at risk, ensuring support was delivered in line with established standards. 38% of identified GBV survivors and persons at risk received case management services, slightly below the 40% target. Services remained survivor-centred, confidential, and timely, including referrals to health, legal, and psychosocial support.
- UNHCR sustained its focus on child protection programming, ensuring that children and adolescents at risk were consistently identified and supported through structured case management interventions. In 2025, 95% of children at risk under case management had individualized case plans developed, fully meeting the annual target. These case plans were developed through a comprehensive process of identification, assessment, referral, and follow-up, guided by the best interests of the child and tailored to the specific vulnerabilities and needs of each case.
